news.body: Key takeaways US authorities filed a civil forfeiture complaint on November 23 seeking more than $1.1 billion in USDC linked to the October 29 Binance hack, across 36 addresses on 18 blockchains. Circle froze the funds but says it cannot technically move them, so it proposes issuing replacement USDC to the US after a forfeiture order. Frozen is not recovered: the filings advance the legal-control stage, while final distribution and ownership remain undecided. news.body: Key takeaways CFTC staff guidance issued on November 23 says swap execution facilities, designated contract markets and clearinghouses may count Bitcoin, Ether and qualifying payment stablecoins toward certain financial resource requirements. The advisory references a minimum 20% haircut for Bitcoin and Ethereum, so a $10 million Bitcoin reserve would count as $8 million, and 2% for qualifying payment stablecoins.
